Section 1: Executive Summary & Operating Reality

C-Suite Executive Verification: Primary SEC 20-F filings and corporate governance documentation confirm that Eddie Wu (Wu Yongming) serves as the active Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Director of Alibaba Group Holding Limited, having assumed leadership in September 2023. Toby Xu (Xu Hong) serves as active Chief Financial Officer (CFO), managing group financial operations since April 2022. Joseph C. Tsai serves as Chairman of the Board of Directors, and J. Michael Evans serves as President. Former CEO Daniel Zhang and former CFO Maggie Wu no longer hold executive operating authority.

Alibaba Group is executing a structural strategic pivot, transitioning from a margin-harvesting digital conglomerate into a hyper-focused AI and core consumption power. Under CEO Eddie Wu's strategic directive, Alibaba is intentionally deploying balance sheet liquidity into two paramount growth pillars: Cloud Intelligence Group (AI + Cloud) and Core Consumption (Taobao & Tmall Group and Taobao Instant Commerce). Recent operating results demonstrate early validation of this thesis: Cloud Intelligence Group external customer revenue accelerated to +40% YoY growth, powered by 11 consecutive quarters of triple-digit growth in AI-related product revenue. Enterprise adoption of Alibaba's proprietary foundation model family, Qwen, alongside Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) infrastructure, has established Alibaba Cloud as the indispensable AI compute layer for the Chinese enterprise ecosystem.

However, this multi-year technology reinvestment phase—backed by a 380 billion RMB three-year AI/cloud CapEx commitment—has compressed short-term reported operating cash flow and GAAP profitability. Operating margins have experienced intentional headwinds as management aggressively subsidies instant commerce unit delivery economics, expands user experience enhancements on Taobao/Tmall, and builds out proprietary AI data centers. While reported operating income declined sharply due to these non-discretionary tech builds and quick-commerce scaling, core underlying organic revenue grew +11% YoY on a like-for-like basis (adjusting for the strategic divestments of legacy brick-and-mortar retail assets Sun Art and Intime Retail). Management remains steadfast that sacrifice of near-term operating cash flows is a deliberate price paid to secure permanent structural moats in generative AI infrastructure and defend domestic market share against aggressive social commerce competitors.

Primary Executive Commentary from Latest Earnings Call:

"AI is and will continue to be one of our primary growth engines. Our Cloud Intelligence Group's revenue accelerated to 38% growth, with external cloud customer revenue up 40% and AI-related product revenue delivering triple-digit growth for the eleventh consecutive quarter. Our Model-as-a-Service platform is emerging as a new engine driving enterprise cloud adoption. On the consumer side, we have integrated Qwen directly into Taobao shopping, enabling users to browse, compare, and manage deliveries via natural conversation. Looking ahead, we are well-positioned to drive growth on both enterprise AI and consumer AI fronts, powered by our full-stack AI capabilities spanning foundation models, cloud infrastructure, and proprietary chips."
— Eddie Wu, Chief Executive Officer

"The rapid growth of AI + Cloud businesses in recent quarters gives us full confidence to scale strategic investments, further strengthening our full-stack AI capabilities. In consumption, our quick commerce business continues to scale rapidly while unit economics improved steadily. Our strong liquidity position and resilient baseline cash generation provide a solid foundation to support sustained strategic investment while returning capital through dividends and buybacks."
— Toby Xu, Chief Financial Officer

Section 2: Business Model Reality, Unit Economics & Competitive Moat

Alibaba Group generates revenue through six distinct operating business units and an investment holding portfolio. The foundational economic engine remains the Taobao & Tmall Group (TTG), which monetizes merchant activity via Customer Management Revenue (CMR)—a high-margin combination of pay-for-performance search marketing, display advertising, commission fees on completed transactions, and merchant software subscriptions. The Cloud Intelligence Group operates on an IaaS/PaaS/MaaS usage-based subscription model, earning recurring revenue from public cloud compute, object storage, database management, and API consumption fees for the Qwen generative AI ecosystem. Alibaba International Digital Commerce (AIDC) monetizes cross-border trade via direct transaction commissions, merchant fulfillment services, and localization logistics across platforms like AliExpress, Lazada, and Trendyol.

Switching Costs & Network Moat Hierarchy: Alibaba's economic moats vary significantly across operating units:

  • Cloud & MaaS Switching Costs (Very High Moat): Moving enterprise IT workloads, custom proprietary databases, and fine-tuned AI workflows off Alibaba Cloud entails immense operational risk, data migration costs, and developer retraining. As China's leading Model-as-a-Service infrastructure, Alibaba Cloud hosts over 50% of China's AI startups and large enterprise AI models, creating a high-margin lock-in effect.
  • Merchant Ecosystem Two-Sided Network Effects (High Moat): With over 1 billion domestic active consumers and millions of active merchants, Taobao/Tmall remains the definitive commercial search engine in China. Merchants cannot afford to exit Taobao due to unmatched purchase intent, consumer review histories, and deeply integrated ERP store management toolchains.
  • Pricing Power Dynamics: While domestic e-commerce take rates faced pricing pressure during intense multi-platform competition, Alibaba retains proven pricing power in enterprise cloud computing (selective price hikes on high-demand AI accelerator clusters) and merchant monetization tools (higher merchant ad adoption driven by AI-powered search targeting).

Secular Tailwinds vs. Structural Disruption Threats

Structural Secular Tailwinds:

  1. Enterprise AI Migration to Cloud: China's rapid corporate adoption of generative AI models requires massive compute clusters. Alibaba Cloud's proprietary Qwen ecosystem position it as the prime beneficiary of China's enterprise digital transformation, converting raw AI model demand into long-term PaaS/IaaS recurring revenue.
  2. Cross-Border Supply Chain Arbitrage: The expansion of AIDC (AliExpress Choice and Trendyol) enables Chinese manufacturers to export directly to global consumers, unlocking structural margin expansion in international trade.
  3. Integration of AI into Consumer E-Commerce: Direct integration of conversational AI search agents (Qwen into Taobao) converts open-ended consumer queries into direct transactional orders, lifting purchase conversion rates and merchant advertising return-on-ad-spend (ROAS).

Competitive Disruption & Substitution Threats:

  1. Social Commerce & Attention Cannibalization: ByteDance's Douyin and Kuaishou continue to capture user screen time, converting traditional search-based intent shopping into impulse video purchases. This forces Alibaba to spend heavily on user subsidies and quick-commerce features to maintain customer engagement frequency.
  2. Price War in Value E-Commerce: PDD Holdings' relentless low-cost positioning forces Taobao to match aggressive merchant subsidies, placing ongoing downward pressure on domestic e-commerce EBITA margins.
  3. Geopolitical Semiconductor Restrictions: Western export controls on advanced AI accelerator hardware (e.g. high-end NVIDIA GPUs) restrict hardware acquisition speed, forcing Alibaba to rely on domestic alternative silicon and soft-architectural software optimizations to sustain its AI compute lead.

Section 3: Forensic Cash Flow, SBC Dilution & Owner Earnings Audit

A rigorous audit of Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE: BABA) requires stripping away management's favored Non-GAAP adjustments, such as Adjusted EBITDA and Non-GAAP Free Cash Flow, which artificially pad reported liquidity by adding back real economic costs. Under the 7 First Principles of Business Valuation, Stock-Based Compensation (SBC) is not a non-cash accounting ghost; it represents an unavoidable equity dilution expense that transfers true economic ownership from public shareholders to employees. To derive true Warren Buffett Owner Earnings, 100% of SBC must be deducted directly from Operating Cash Flow alongside defensive Maintenance CapEx.

Furthermore, evaluating Alibaba's cash flow requires isolating discretionary growth capital investments—specifically the massive infrastructure outlay for AI servers, hyperscale data center construction, and Qwen model training clusters—from basic operational moat maintenance. In FY 2026, management accelerated AI CapEx significantly, suppressing headline Free Cash Flow while building scalable computing infrastructure.

Discretionary Growth CapEx surged from $2,528M in FY 2024 to $14,569M in FY 2026 as Cloud Intelligence Group expanded graphics processing units (GPUs) and liquid-cooled data center facilities. Section 5: Warren Buffett Owner Earnings Intrinsic Valuation Matrix

To evaluate Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE: BABA) through an unyielding value investing lens, we discard Wall Street's promotional Non-GAAP EBITDA and superficial revenue multiples. True enterprise value lies solely in the cash that can be extracted from the business over its remaining operating lifespan, discounted back to the present. Following Warren Buffett's 1986 Shareholder Letter methodology, we derive True Owner Earnings by starting with GAAP Operating Cash Flow, subtracting 100% of Stock-Based Compensation (SBC) as an indisputable economic cash expense, and bifurcating Capital Expenditures between defensive Maintenance CapEx and discretionary Growth CapEx.

The 1986 Owner Earnings Derivation Formula:
Owner Earnings = GAAP Operating Cash Flow - Maintenance CapEx - 100% Stock-Based Compensation

For Alibaba's trailing twelve months, reported GAAP Operating Cash Flow stands at $23.85 Billion. We deduct $2.70 Billion in Stock-Based Compensation (which dilutes shareholder equity if unsterilized) and isolate $4.15 Billion in Maintenance CapEx required to preserve Taobao/Tmall infrastructure, Cainiao fulfillment nodes, and server refreshes. We exclude $9.50 Billion in discretionary growth CapEx directed toward AI clusters (NVIDIA/H20 and proprietary T-Head processors) and hyperscale cloud expansion. This yields a Normalized Base Case Owner Earnings figure of $17.00 Billion ($7.09 per ADS).

Local Sovereign Discount Rate Derivation

In accordance with the PetroChina and Iscar local sovereign hurdle rate principles, international cash flows generated predominantly in Renminbi (RMB) must never be discounted using US Treasury yields. Instead, the discount rate is anchored to the local benchmark:

  • Base Currency Benchmark: China 10-Year Government Bond Yield = 1.68%
  • Equity Risk Premium (ERP): Adjusted for Chinese macroeconomic volatility, foreign exchange controls, and variable interest entity (VIE) structural complexity = 6.82%
  • Required Hurdle Rate (Discount Rate): 1.68% + 6.82% = 8.50%

If the New York Stock Exchange and Hong Kong Stock Exchange were to close permanently for 5 years, an owner purchasing Alibaba in its entirety today at a $298.8 Billion market capitalization ($240.8 Billion Enterprise Value) would collect approximately $93.5 Billion in cumulative organic Owner Earnings over the 5-year period under Base Case parameters.
